decisions.decision: Vapi remains the voice runtime; Xphere supplies internal specialist orchestration and actions.
decisions.rationale: Preserves proven telephony while sharing business intelligence across channels.

decisions.decision: Voice and text reuse the same specialist agents through channel policies.
decisions.rationale: Avoids duplicated prompts, tools, drift, and per-channel agent forks.

decisions.decision: All Xphere-owned generative inference routes through OpenRouter.
decisions.rationale: Centralizes provider policy and tenant/platform fallback; embeddings remain a separate compatibility decision.

decisions.decision: Action Engine remains the authoritative provider execution path.
decisions.rationale: Protects the core multi-tenant platform invariant.

decisions.decision: Cuts & Culture is a late isolated canary, not a platform default.
decisions.rationale: Avoids hardcoding one tenant's operating model into the product.

decisions.decision: Legacy non-workflow tools are never delegable and fail closed through a partner edge.
decisions.rationale: Migration 1291 keys delegated grants to workflows, so legacy tools have no grant surface to check; inferring authority would break least privilege.

decisions.decision: Trusted specialist routing resolves before invokeAgent rather than inside it.
decisions.rationale: The gateway contract asserts that input.intent never influences trusted identity; resolving inside would break it.

decisions.decision: The idempotency preflight fails closed on infrastructure error.
decisions.rationale: A lookup that could not complete means we do not know whether a prior attempt already mutated the provider; executing anyway is the double-booking the phase exists to prevent.

decisions.decision: A failure to persist the idempotency receipt never downgrades a completed mutation to an error.
decisions.rationale: The caller would hear a failure for work that landed, and the real result would be lost.

next_action: Migrations are applied. Everything else remains on the human gate in docs/agents/canary-activation-runbook.md - start at step 2 (the provisioning dry run). Step 5.0, rewiring an ingress route to invokeAgentWithChannelRouting, is the one that makes the routing switch mean anything.
context_notes: All 6 phases (131-136) built and verified. What is LIVE today: everything phases 132-134 put inside runAgent and /api/vapi/tools - edge-based least privilege, kb_scope, partner_calls, denial recording, redaction before persistence, and the idempotency guard. The widget route calls runAgent directly so it inherits these. What is NOT live: the Phase 131 gateway, Phase 132 specialist routing and the Phase 134 channel switch - invokeAgent has zero production callers. Release gate: npm run release-gate (8 suites, 206 tests + 33 workflow validations), CI at .github/workflows/release-gate.yml. Full-suite baseline is ~30 failing files for live-DB and module-resolution reasons - but note that one of those was a real security leak, so audit newcomers rather than assuming noise. Build needs NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192; a local Redis on localhost:6379 being down makes static generation slow and flaky but it passes on retry. Never junction node_modules into a git worktree.
